title: Shahchippitchage Boundary Stones
summary: Shahchippitchage is a Montauk boundary-mark name for a pile of stones in North Neck, in the land between Fort Pond and Lake Montauk.
history_content: The name belongs to a set of 1670 Montauk boundary descriptions connected with the Nine Score Acre Purchase. The modern pin is a broad placement between the ponds, not the exact location of the stone marker.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Shahchippitchage and Shahchippetchuge. The name is interpreted as meaning the midway place of separation.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names do more than label streets—they encode the priorities of the institutions that assign them.”

— Ye Tian, The Functional Priority of Memory: Critical Toponymy and Selective Heritage-Making (2026), Abstract
preservation_content: Shahchippitchage preserves how Native place-names could mark boundaries, paths, and remembered land divisions as well as villages or water features.
